clue.text: Turn to person of importance making a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: A visit to an important figure staging a return to public life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns TOVIP (TO plus VIP) end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to swivel or rotate on a central point, a synonym for turning.

clue.text: Pictures of, say, Liverpool river as it develops

parts.note: Liverpool is an example of a port, signalled by say

indicators.note: develops means changing into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paintings of the River Mersey at Liverpool as it changes over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' rearranges AS IT to AITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Portraits are pictures, usually of people.

clue.text: Loud salvo calculated to conceal it

indicators.note: the two words conceal the answer inside them, running from the end of one into the next

explanation.surface: A burst of gunfire that was designed to cover something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocal means outspoken, voiced loudly and openly.

clue.text: Announce utter chaos surrounding elected member

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the elected member
chaos suggests disorder, so the word utter is rearranged

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: An MP is caught in total disorder and must make a statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos' turns UTTER into TRUET, which goes 'surrounding' MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to proclaim it loudly, as a herald announces.

clue.text: Reserves unlikely retail outlet

parts.note: to reserve a table or seat is to book it, so reserves gives books
a tall story is an unlikely one, so tall can mean improbable

explanation.surface: Stockpiles held by an improbable kind of shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand selling books and papers, as at a station, is a kind of shop or retail outlet.

clue.text: Singles may offer these as well, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word sounds like the one heard aloud

parts.note: besides means in addition, as well

explanation.surface: Records released as singles also come with something extra.
explanation.walkthrough: On old vinyl singles the main track was the A-side and the secondary track the B-side.
explanation.definitionFit: A single record carries a lesser track on its reverse, the flip side.

clue.text: Finished article in bed: 'What Not to Wear!'

parts.note: over means finished, ended

indicators.note: in means the article goes inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A finished item in bed refers to the TV makeover show What Not to Wear.
explanation.walkthrough: What Not to Wear was a British TV fashion show; here, a coat is something you would not wear in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcoat is outerwear you would hardly put on in bed, a playful clue to a garment.

clue.text: Disappointment resulting from poor bet in bed

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the bed word

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed, as in hitting the sack

indicators.note: poor suggests something badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Regret after making a bad wager from under the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges BET to ETB, placed 'in' SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reversal of progress, a let-down.

clue.text: A new suggestion on poems in Australia for example

indicators.note: on means placed next to, the pieces being joined in order

parts.note: a tip is a hint or suggestion
odes are lyrical poems

explanation.surface: A fresh idea about poetry from Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: From a British viewpoint Australia and New Zealand are the Antipodes, being on the opposite side of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes are lands diametrically opposite, a term used in Britain for Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Attracted by endless plum wine, for example

indicators.note: endless means the word loses both its ends, leaving the middle

parts.note: red is a kind of wine

explanation.surface: Drawn in by a never-ending plum wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lured means enticed or tempted, drawn in as by bait.

clue.text: Scoop in which soldiers replace former lover wanting to be alone

indicators.note: the soldiers take the place of the former lover inside the scoop word

parts.note: a newspaper scoop is an exclusive story
an ex is a former partner
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A newspaper story where troops stand in for someone's old flame who craves solitude.
explanation.walkthrough: In EXCLUSIVE, 'replace' swaps the EX at the front for RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse shuns company, so being reclusive means preferring solitude.

clue.text: Regularly taunt poor person providing instruction

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the following words, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone keeps mocking a poor wretch who teaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of 'taunt poor' give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher who gives lessons is a person who provides instruction.

clue.text: Runs circuits in case of extreme deterioration in health

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: the circuits are placed inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: laps are circuits of a track

explanation.surface: Someone running laps while extremely unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of extreme' is E and E, and 'in' puts LAPS between them after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into illness after seeming to recover.

clue.text: Constricted by muscular affliction?

definitions.meaning: confined, with little room to move
affected by cramp, a painful muscle spasm, which the question mark marks as playful

explanation.definitionFit: Cramped means short of space, and also literally suffering from cramp in the muscles.

clue.text: Ask for strangely inactive account to be deleted

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the word inactive are rearranged
deleted says the account letters are removed from the shuffled pool

explanation.surface: Someone asks a bank to close an oddly dormant account.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AC out of INACTIVE ('to be deleted') and rearrange what is left, VEINIT ('strangely'), into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To invite someone is to ask them to come, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Flexible, but nasty having to accept variable rates

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the jumbled letters go inside

parts.note: vile means nasty

indicators.note: variable means changeable, so the letters of rates change order

explanation.surface: A deal with flexible terms that is unpleasant because of fluctuating interest rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' signals the anagram and 'having to accept' the container: the nasty word takes the rearranged letters in. The surface's 'variable rates' reads like a mortgage.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatile means adaptable to many uses, the sense of flexible.

clue.text: All ready to go away, and well-informed — and broke down!

parts.note: with bags packed, ready for a trip
to be well up on a subject is to know it well

explanation.surface: Someone ready for a holiday, clued up, and then the car fails.
explanation.definitionFit: When a machine packs up, it stops working, the same idiom as breaking down.

clue.text: Carry on through cut on energy

indicators.note: on means the next piece follows the previous one

parts.note: per means through or by, as in per post
to sever is to cut
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Keep going despite a reduction in power.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to persist, carrying on despite difficulty.

clue.text: Vault across bull without protection of mobile phone

indicators.note: the vault reaches across, spanning the inner letters

parts.note: a cellar is an underground vault

indicators.note: with no protection means stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: Leaping over a bull without padding while on a mobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without protection' strips BULL to UL, set 'across' by CELLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellular phone is a mobile phone, which works through a network of cells.

clue.text: Vessel crossing river shows flag

indicators.note: the vessel goes across, that is around, the river letter

parts.note: a steamer is a steam-powered ship

explanation.surface: A boat crossing a river is flying colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' places R inside STEAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant.

clue.text: A small capacity left to cover America's charge

indicators.note: the outer pieces cover the American part on both sides, enclosing it

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a small measure of capacity
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A small venue left to deal with an accusation against the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: ACCL goes round USA, with USA placed before the final L.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusal is an accusation, the act of charging someone.

clue.text: Unsuccessful gambler chasing source of cash getting nearer

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the gambler comes after
the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: a loser is someone who loses a bet

explanation.surface: A losing punter going after money draws closer.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer is the comparative of close, meaning nearer in distance.

clue.text: A cursory examination appears evasive, superficially

parts.note: looks means appears, as in looks tired

indicators.note: superficially means just the surface of the word, its outer letters

explanation.surface: A brief glance comes across as shifty on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superficially' takes the outer letters of 'evasive', E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is an informal quick inspection or glance.

clue.text: Tree legislation turns head

indicators.note: turns means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: law is legislation
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A new law changes someone's mind about a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The walnut is a tree that bears edible nuts.

clue.text: Area of church making gambler change sides, finally

indicators.note: the last letter, R for right, swaps to L for left, switching side

parts.note: a chancer takes risks, like a gambler

explanation.surface: A church setting where a punter switches allegiance at the last.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) at the end of CHANCER becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, used by clergy and choir.

clue.text: Pack diamonds into vehicles

indicators.note: into means the diamond letter goes inside the vehicles

parts.note: cars are vehicles
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Load jewels into cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack is a set of playing cards, a deck.

clue.text: One's expectations initially after a cat spray

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the a-and-cat part

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
one's read as one is, I'S, giving IS

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word expectations

explanation.surface: Someone's hopes for a cat spraying its territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is I'S, I being one, giving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To atomise a liquid is to turn it into a fine spray, as an atomiser does.

clue.text: Some basic ingredients in cakes?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking what elementary components go into cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a sweet coating that is part of many cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar topping is found on and between layers of many cakes, so it is something in cakes.

clue.text: Means of controlling rinse cycles

indicators.note: cycles suggests going round and mixing, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Settings for washing-machine rinse programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the straps a rider uses to control a horse, so a means of control.

clue.text: Overwhelming victory for transparency by nation

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a land is a country or nation
a slide is a photographic transparency for projecting

explanation.surface: A projected image placed alongside a country in a winning result.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is an election win by a huge margin.

clue.text: Suspect everybody returned in term as planned

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed inside the rearranged letters
planned is read as having been arranged or designed, so the letters are reshuffled
returned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone came back during the academic term as scheduled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives LLA, which goes 'in' SMERAT, an arrangement of TERM AS ('planned').
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom for suspecting that something is wrong.

clue.text: Almost keen to embrace Lincoln's first symbol of America

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other
almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: eager means keen

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Lincoln

explanation.surface: Eagerness to honour Abraham Lincoln's leading emblem of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts EAGER to EAGE; L goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is the national bird and emblem of the United States.
